S.MANIKUMAR, C.J.

For information purpose only Instant writ petition is filed seeking for direction to the respondents to verify the licence of unauthorised packaged drinking water units in the state and refuse the licence of these unauthorized units in the Kerala State.
On 8th February 2021, this court passed the following order:

The petitioner, Human Rights Mission, claiming to be a registered society, has filed this writ petition challenging the action of the unauthorised packaged drinking water units and ice units to prevent companies from unauthorised distribution of polluted water and ice bars in the Kerala State.
2. Respondent No.6, Bureau of Indian Standards, has filed a counter affidavit.

However, respondent Nos. 1 to 5 have not filed any counter affidavit or statement of facts, setting out the steps taken to verify the licence of unauthorised packaged drinking water units and the consequential action under the statutory provisions, namely, the Prevention of Food Adulteration Rules, 1955 and Bureau of Indian Standards Act.

3. Sri. Surin George Ipe, learned Special Government Pleader, contended that there is nothing to support the contention of the petitioner that the petitioner, namely, the Human Rights Mission, is a registered society under the Registration Act.

4. Having regard to the subject issue, namely, prevention and taking adequate action against the unauthorised distribution of polluted water and ice bars in the Kerala State, we deem it fit to convert the writ petition, as a suo motu Public Interest Litigation.
The writ petition has already been assigned number and therefore, fresh exercise is required.

5. Learned Senior Government Pleader is directed to file a consolidated statement of facts/counter affidavit, as the case may be setting out the action taken with reference to the prayers sought for,
with supporting documents.

counter details be filed.
